messages:
incident-bot: Paging SRE rotation: multiple client TLS handshake failures observed for hosted API in eu-west-1. Severity: Sev2. Trigger: 5xx rate on /v1/generate + connection errors. Alert: https://console.redwood/alerts/18923
Maya: I got the page, on it. Saw spike at 12:08 UTC. Lots of `handshake failure` in the fronting ALB logs.
Ashwin: I'm on-call. Pulling ALB logs and edge TLS metrics now.
Chris: Adding context — we shipped a cert rotation job at 11:55 UTC for eu-west-1 that rotated both ALB and ingress certificates. Could be related.
Linh: Noted. Are customers seeing 5xx or connection resets? Any specific client errors?
Diego: Customer support reports timeouts and "TLS handshake" errors for multiple customers starting ~12:06. Replicated via curl from my laptop to the API endpoint: `curl https://api.eu.redwood.example/v1/ -v` shows `SSL handshake failed`.
Maya: Timeline so far:
- 11:55 UTC: cert rotation job kicked off
- 12:06 UTC: first alert firing (handshake errors)
- 12:08 UTC: SEV2 page
- 12:10 UTC: team assembled in thread
Ashwin: Quick checks I'm running:
- `aws elbv2 describe-listeners --load-balancer-arn <alb>`
- `openssl s_client -connect api.eu.redwood.example:443 -servername api.eu.redwood.example -showcerts`
- `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/ingress-controller --since=20m`
Maya: OpenSSL output (from my laptop):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139820... error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
---
no peer certificate available
```
Chris: Ingress logs show repeated `tls: handshake failure from x.x.x.x: remote error: tls: bad certificate` entries at 12:06-12:09.
Linh: ALB access logs show 502 with `SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE` code. Putting a copy here: 
```
time 2026-03-15T12:06:35Z elb alb-1 10.0.0.1:443 10.0.2.4:32768 0.000 0.020 502 SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE "GET /v1/generate"
```
Ashwin: Hypotheses (initial):
- H1: New certs missing intermediate or wrong chain deployed to ALB (cert chain issue)
- H2: Ingress certs not rotated (mismatch between ALB and backend cert chain causing ALB->backend validation failures)
- H3: MTU/fragmentation on peered VPC path causing truncated TLS ClientHello -> handshake fails
- H4: SNI mismatch / wrong domain on cert
Maya: Let's mark H1/H2 as highest probability given rotation job just ran. Running `aws acm describe-certificate` and checking certificate IDs used by ALB.
Diego: I pulled the cert IDs. ALB listener points to cert arn: arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:...:certificate/abcd-rotated
ACM cert metadata shows: `status: ISSUED`, `notAfter: 2028-02-01` — not expired. Chain: intermediate present in ACM UI.
Chris: Ingress controller (nginx) still serving an older cert according to `kubectl exec` and reading `/etc/ssl/certs/tls.crt` — shows subject CN=api.redwood.internal and SANs without public domain. That looks like the backend wasn't updated.
Ashwin: That aligns with H2 — ALB has new public cert, backend still has internal cert causing ALB->backend TLS to fail if ALB is set to use HTTPS backend with strict validation.
Linh: Check ALB target group protocol — is it HTTPS with `validate target health` enabled? If so, ALB will validate cert chain.
Maya: ALB target group configured with `HTTPS` and `health check` uses `HTTPS` default. There's a setting `server_name`? It's set to `instance-id` no custom. So ALB is doing TLS to backend and likely failing.
Diego: From ALB logs where backend returned 502, there are instances of `upstream_ssl_alert_received:47` meaning backend sent Alert 47 (unknown CA?) — unsure mapping.
Ashwin: Let's try a direct TLS handshake from ALB instance to backend pod (using `aws ssm` into node). If node can't validate backend cert, that'll confirm.
Chris: I ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.2.4:8443 -servername api.eu.redwood.example -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt -showcerts` and got:
```
Verification error: unable to verify the first certificate
```
Maya: That's H2 confirmed. Backend is serving a cert not chain-trusted by ALB.
Linh: Why did backend not rotate? Deployment job should have updated ingress pods. Last deploy for ingress helm release shows success at 11:50. But cert sync job ran later at 11:55.
Diego: Possible race: cert rotation job updated ACM and ALB listener first, then attempted to roll ingress, but helm chart check failed for one replica and left older pods.
Ashwin: Let's check pods: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=ingress -o wide` — one pod is on node with image tag older.
Chris: One ingress replica crashed due to OOM earlier at 11:52 (we have crashloopbackoff). It never restarted into the new rollout and is running older image with old cert mount.
Maya: Action: scale up new ingress replicas and force rollout to pick new cert secret. Running: `kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/ingress-controller` and `kubectl -n prod scale deploy/ingress-controller --replicas=4`.
Linh: I'll temporarily change ALB target group protocol to HTTP for routing to allow traffic while we finish rotation, but that's a risky change. Thoughts?
Ashwin: If we switch to HTTP, client TLS still terminates at ALB, so customer TLS still works. But we may break any backend auth that expects TLS. We need to check if any inter-service mTLS depends on HTTPS path.
Diego: Customer-facing path ok if ALB terminates TLS for us. No mTLS between ALB and backend currently in prod except optional backend cert validation (we have it turned on). Changing to HTTP will bypass backend validation.
Chris: I vote to flip to HTTP target temporarily to restore traffic, then rotate backend cert and re-enable HTTPS. Will schedule rollback if problems.
Maya: Doing change now: switching target group protocol to HTTP. ETA 2 minutes.
incident-bot: Change recorded by Maya at 12:23 UTC. https://console.redwood/changes/4571
Ashwin: Health checks are green now, 200s returning from targets.
Diego: Client errors dropping. Monitoring shows error rate back to normal baseline at 12:26.
Maya: Great. Now finish backend cert rotation and ensure pods mount correct certs. Rolling restart completed at 12:30. Verifying with `openssl s_client` from node to pod shows full chain validated.
Chris: Re-enabled HTTPS on ALB target group at 12:35 and set health check to HTTPS. ALB logs show no more SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE and 200s.
Linh: Root cause hypothesis: cert rotation order and a partial rollout left some backends with old/internal certs while ALB served new public cert, causing ALB->backend validation failures. Secondary contributor: a single crashed ingress replica prevented full rollout.
Ashwin: We'll mark H2 as primary and H3 (MTU) as unrelated after tcpdump check — no ICMP fragmentation or dropped fragments observed.
Maya: Short-term mitigation: revert to HTTP during rotation next time, or ensure certs rotate backend-first. Also add a canary check to verify backend cert chain before swapping ALB listener cert.
Diego: Action items (owners):
- Chris: write post-incident RCA draft with timeline + root cause (due EOD) 
- Ashwin: add a preflight check to rotation job that validates all ingress pods have the expected cert chain before updating ALB (PR#342) (due +2d)
- Maya: add automatisms to scale up ingress replicas during rotations to avoid rollout stalls (PR#344) (due +3d)
- Linh: update runbook to include temp HTTP fallback step and clear criteria for use (due +1d)
- Diego: follow up with Support to notify impacted customers and confirm resolution (now)
Maya: Postmortem notes to include logs: ALB logs, ingress pod logs, cert rotation job logs + SSM command outputs. Links: https://console.redwood/logs/alb/18923, https://console.redwood/logs/ingress/18923
Ashwin: Tags for RCA: root_cause:cert_rotation_order, contributing:crashloop_inreplica, mitigation:targetgroup_http_fallback
Chris: I'm adding this thread to the incident timeline doc and will start drafting. Anyone else need to add context?
Diego: I'll ping Finance for potential credit to impacted customers.
Maya: Closing page to SEV3 at 12:40 UTC. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Closed pager at 12:40 UTC.
Linh: Quick note: add an automated smoke test that runs `openssl s_client` from a node to each ingress pod when we do future rotations.
Ashwin: Agree. Also add a check in CI for ACM cert chain completeness.
Maya: Thanks all. Moving to post-incident channel for the writeup. 
Chris: Thanks — great coordination. :thumbsup:
